messages:
anita: quick sync — proposing a new "flow-control surface" for tenant-level backpressure. idea: expose a small set of knobs (soft_limit, trial_rate, abuse_override) at the control-plane API so product/platform can tune without infra deploys. want feedback on tradeoffs and interface boundaries.

devon: can you sketch the API payload? also how would this interact with existing token-bucket admission?

anita: yep — high-level sketch below. the goal is to be conservative: defaults keep current behavior, explicit fields opt-in.

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "flow_control": {
    "mode": "soft",          // soft | hard | shadow
    "soft_limit_rps": 20,     // target requests/sec (best-effort)
    "trial_rate": 0.1,        // fraction of requests allowed to burst beyond soft_limit
    "abuse_override": "auto" // auto | score_threshold | off
  }
}
```

kai: looks reasonable. two immediate concerns: 1) soft vs hard semantics can be confusing to client teams. 2) telemetry surface — we need per-tenant time-series for effective rate, trial-hit, and enforced-drop to prove it's safe.

anita: agreed. proposal: soft mode emits advisory responses with header X-Flow-Status: advisory and includes heuristic reason; hard mode returns 429. shadow mode records signals only. we will add metrics: flow.soft_target, flow.actual_rps, flow.trial_allowed, flow.drops, flow.abuse_overrides.

sasha: about abuse_override:auto — what triggers it? we have separate abuse signal pipeline (abuse_score). auto would trigger when abuse_score > threshold AND unusual burst pattern. need explicit contract with eng-security about latency/opacity of that signal.

anita: yes — auto means control-plane consults a cached abuse_score service (50ms p95 extra). if not available, behavior defaults to soft. we should allow product teams to pin to score_threshold numbers or set off.

devon: implementation-wise, do we want to implement this in the admission path (fast, in path to token-bucket) or as a router-level prefilter that annotates requests and then admission consults annotation?

kai: router-level prefilter preferred — isolates abuse lookup and lets admission focus on tokens. prefilter can also do sampling for trial_rate and tag KV cache keys for batching. downside: more moving parts, cross-service contract.

anita: I lean router-prefilter too. simpler to iterate and we can run shadow-mode globally to validate signals. plan: land API surface, wire router-prefilter + metrics, rollout in shadow, then enable soft defaults for a small org set.

ops-bot: deploy:flow-control-prefilter job started for cluster-us-west-2 by anita — build/4572 -> staging.

devon: rollout checklist please: 1) docs for product teams, 2) dashboards, 3) eviction safety test (simulated heavy tenants), 4) playbook for rollback.

anita: adding to plan. I'll open RFC follow-up PR with interface docs, migration guide, and test harness. if no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll start the PR.

sasha: flagging eng-security to join RFC follow-up: @devon can you loop them in?

devon: on it. looping @sec-team.

anita: thanks all — trying to keep this minimal and low-risk. happy to sync 30m if helpful.
